title: The bird · first page
logline: A small rainbow bird on the seawall, wrong for the coast. Not explained. It stays.

panels.composition: The seawall, May morning. WOOD from behind on the wall with BARNABY II. Three feet away, where the crow was in July: a small plump bird, teal head, rose breast, green wing, long teal tail. A painted bunting. The only saturated color on the page. Wood's head turned toward it, just; we see the side of his jaw. The pup hasn't noticed.

image.prompt: a man seen from behind sitting on a stone seawall with a three-legged dog, his head turned slightly toward a small plump rainbow songbird perched three feet away on the wall, the bird the only saturated color on a page of muted slate and ochre watercolor, no panel borders, no words
image.notes: The bird replaces the crow's spot. Never explained. The afterword will have to speak to it.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The Bird sequence begins. Where the crow was.
